One English typescript letter sheet with a handwritten place/date, salutation, one continuous body paragraph, corrections, and a bottom marginal note. No signature or own page number appears. Archive 21 is not treated as the author’s pagination.
The place remains doubtful Massy; the date reads 22. 10. 1969. The two article names occur as quoted references within the letter, not as a page title.

The writer requests later reprints and says the work calls for reconsideration in algebraic geometry. The letter states conjugacy counts for quadruples of tori and Borel groups and a stabilizer assertion.

The explicit hesitations are retained: I wonder if you know the answer to some of them; for some, or for all; Is there in any sense a distinguished conjugacy class; and What are the groups of automorphisms. These are questions, not proven conclusions.
The last sentence ends at (they on this sheet. No continuation was consulted or supplied.
The bottom note states a normalizer-intersection extension and its order. Its small annotation identifies the final Z as center of G-tilde. The rightmost order is written on a second, lower row.
Shared witness forms were checked too: suggests number has no article; polynomail preserves ai with a pen transposition; stablity lacks the expected i. No grammatical repairs were made.

The source geometry, rather than expected spelling, prompted retaining a graphic r/k cell and a typewriter k/i overlay without inventing chronology. Body phi, underlined typed Z, and handwritten double-stroke Z were read locally.
